references.text: In John 12:9-11, it is described how the people and chief priests again look for Jesus in Jerusalem in connection with the feast, and plan to kill him. This is a direct continuation of the scene in 11:56 where they are looking for him in the temple.

In Matthew 21:45-46, the chief priests and Pharisees look for a way to seize Jesus, but fear the crowd. This mirrors the motif in John 11:56 where they look for him in the temple and discuss whether he will come, with the same intention of capturing him.

Mark 11:18 describes how the chief priests and scribes look for a way to destroy Jesus while they are in the temple. This is a parallel event to John 11:56 where they stand in the temple and discuss his arrival at the feast.
